items.title: Section: Momentum, Sustaining, and Diminishment — And Why Matter Is Still "Made" by the Elements Even Though It Arises From Its Own Seed

items.zh: 又由先業勢所引故，內諸色處差別而生。又復諸天或現前欲、或不現前欲，及北拘盧洲所有資具，當知多分勢引而生，差別而轉。人中相續生者，唯有器世界。如是等類，當知名勢引生。云何攝受生？謂遇彼彼攝受緣故，彼彼色法展轉增益勝上而生，猶如水等潤萌芽等。如是等類，名攝受生。與此相違，應知名損減生。復次，諸聚色生時，如種種物石磨為末，以水和合，團雜而生，非如苣蕂、麥、豆等聚。何以故？隨彼生因增上力故，如是而生，為有用故。問：若一切行皆自種子所生，何因緣故說諸大種造所造色？答：由彼變異而變異故，彼所建立及任持故。由三因緣大種變異，令所造色變異而轉。一、士夫用故；二、業所作故；三、由勝定故。士夫用者，謂由地大所打觸故，器差別故，田差別故，令所造色變異可得。或由水所潤等，火所熟等，風所燥等，令所造色變異可得。當知是名由彼大種士夫用故，令所造色變異而生。業所作者，隨業勢力，先大種生；後隨彼力，色變異生。是名業所作故。由勝定者，勝定力故，先起大種，然後造色變異而生。當知是名由勝定故大種變異，因此造色變異而生。復次，略由五緣，所有大種令其異果轉成異果。何等為五？一、大種力故；二、士夫用力故；三、明呪力故；四、神通力故；五、業所作力故。
items.en:
Furthermore, through the power of prior karma, the internal sense-fields arise with their own distinctions... continuous arising among humans consists only of the physical world. What is arising through sustaining? It is various forms of matter growing progressively stronger and more excellent upon meeting a favourable condition, as water nourishes a sprout. The opposite of this should be known as arising through diminishment.
Question: if all conditioned phenomena arise from their own seed, why is it said that the elements produce derived matter? Answer: because as the elements change, derived matter changes accordingly, being established and sustained by them. Through three causes the elements change, causing derived matter to change in turn: through human effort, through karmic action, and through superior meditative power.
Furthermore, briefly, five conditions cause the elements' already-produced results to transform further into different results: the elements' own force, human effort, the power of spells, supernatural power, and karmic force.

items.title: Section: Not an Echo, Not a Reflection, Not Mere Grasping — Why the Intermediate Being Must Truly Exist

items.zh: 問：從此沒已，何因、何緣中有色聚續得生耶？答：當知此色用自種子為因，感生業為緣。問：何因得知有中有耶？答：從此沒已，若無所依，諸心心所無有道理轉至餘方故。不應如響，唯惑亂故；不應如影，彼不滅故；亦不應說如取所緣，非行往故，由如是等所說譬喻不應道理，是故當知定有中有。
items.en:
Question: after passing from this life, by what cause and condition does the intermediate-state cluster of matter continue to arise? Answer: one should know this matter has its own seed as cause and the karma generating rebirth as condition.
Question: by what reason can one know there is an intermediate state? Answer: after passing from this life, without a physical basis, mind and its mental factors would have no coherent way of transferring elsewhere. It should not be compared to an echo, which is merely illusory; nor to a reflection, since a reflection's original does not cease; nor should it be said to be like mere grasping of an object, since this involves no actual travelling. Since the comparisons stated do not hold, one should definitely know there is an intermediate state.

items.zh: 如是等類，應當思惟色蘊生起。

items.title: Section: Which Element Claims the Space First, and Why Sound Behaves Like a Sudden Flash of Light

items.zh: 復次，色蘊生時，誰為先首據其處所，依此處所餘色轉耶？當知大種先據處所，後餘造色依此處轉。唯諸大種於此處所現前障礙，所餘造色自相遍滿。當知由彼勢力任持，有所據礙。復次，地等諸四大種，隨其次第，麁顯應知。謂地界及果，能持最勝；水、火、風等，流潤、燒然、動搖等業，依止彼故方得流轉。復次，諸聲纔宣發已，尋即斷滅，故於色聚中不恒相續。又此音聲依質生時，質處及外俱頓可得。隨所聞處，於此處所遍滿頓起，如焰光明，非漸漸生展轉往趣。
items.en:
Furthermore, when form aggregate arises, which takes hold of the location first, so that other matter arises depending on this location? One should know the elements take hold of the location first, other derived matter then occurring dependent on this same location. Only the elements are present there as obstruction, other derived matter's own characteristic filling this space completely — one should know this is sustained by their power, occupying it as obstruction. Furthermore, the four elements manifest in sequence from coarse to subtle: the earth-element and its result serve as the most supreme support, water, fire, and wind then flowing, burning, and moving in dependence on it.
Furthermore, sounds, the moment they are uttered, immediately cease, and so do not continuously persist within a cluster of matter. Also, when this sound arises depending on its source, it can be obtained both at the source's own location and elsewhere at once. Wherever it is heard, it arises there suddenly and completely, like a flame's brightness, not arising gradually and spreading outward.

items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Wind — The Cosmic Wheel, the Passing Breeze, and the Breath That Never Stops

items.zh: 復次，風有二種。謂恒相續、不恒相續。諸輪行風，名恒相續；在空行者，名不恒相續。在物行者，名恒攝受。又當知風機關運轉，名恒相續；所餘，當知非恒相續。
items.en: Furthermore, wind is of two kinds: constantly continuous and not constantly continuous. Wind belonging to the wheels is called constantly continuous; wind occurring in open space is called not constantly continuous. Wind present within a body is called constant sustaining. One should also know that wind captured by a mechanism is called constantly continuous; the rest should be known as not constantly continuous.

items.title: Section: Space Itself Is Made of Light and Dark, and Shape Is Nothing But a Convenient Comparison

items.zh: 答：明闇所攝造色，說名空界。此亦二種。一、恒相續，二、不恒相續。若諸有情所居處所常闇常明，名恒相續；餘不爾處，非恒相續。當知此亦依止色聚。又此空界，光明攝者，名為清淨；隙穴攝者，名不清淨。問：諸長短等所說形色，當言實有，為假有耶？答：當言假有。何以故？積集而住，故名為形。唯有眾色積集可得，餘形色相不可得故。又必相待。相待之法有自性者，彼法便有雜亂過失。又如車等，彼覺可壞故。
items.en:
Answer: derived matter subsumed under light and darkness is called space. This too is of two kinds: constantly continuous and not constantly continuous. Where beings dwell in constant darkness or constant light, this is called constantly continuous; elsewhere, not constantly continuous. Space subsumed under light is called pure; subsumed under a crack or hollow, impure. One should know this too depends on a cluster of matter.
Question: are shapes such as long and short genuinely real or merely provisional? Answer: they are provisional. Why? Because they name an accumulated arrangement — only an accumulation of various matter can be found, no further characteristic of shape being findable apart from it. Also, because they are necessarily relative — if a relative phenomenon possessed its own fixed essence, it would fall into contradiction. Also, because, as with a chariot and the like, the notion of it can be destroyed.

blocks.text: How the elements relate to derived form, why the intermediate being is real, and why shape is only a name.

Derived form changes as the elements change, and is established and sustained by them. The conditions: human effort, karma, and superior absorption. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first two belong to the desire realm; the third is the work of absorption.

Master Cháng Bǎi: mind cannot pass to rebirth without the support of form; and if the former body has ceased, there is nothing to cast a shadow. So the intermediate being is not a reflection or an echo.

The elements occupy a location first, and derived form arises dependent on it. Master Cháng Bǎi: 界 here is seed, 果 the manifest mark; earth is coarsest, wind subtlest. Sound "arises wherever it is heard, suddenly and completely, like a flame's brightness". (Untranslated, 0599a14: "in this way one should reflect on how the form aggregate arises.")

The space-element is derived form seen as light and dark. Master Cháng Bǎi: we know space through light and dark. Shape is provisional: take the chariot apart, and the cognition of "chariot" is gone. (Untranslated, 0599b02: "What is the space-element?")
Sound appears all at once where it is heard, not spreading like water. The treatise's physics is careful to describe experience as it is given.

quiz.q: If all conditioned phenomena arise from their own seed, why say the elements produce derived matter?
options: because the elements are the seeds of derived matter, which has no seeds of its own and comes wholly from them
because the scriptures say so, needing no reason
because the elements precede derived matter by one lifetime
because derived matter changes as the elements change, and is established and sustained by them
quiz.why: The treatise answers that derived matter changes as the elements change, and is established and sustained by them. Master Cháng Bǎi: derived matter is established and sustained by the four elements; so although the form aggregate comes from seeds, it is still said to be produced by earth, water, fire, and wind. Seed and elements thus play different roles.

quiz.q: Through which three causes do the elements change, and which two pertain to the desire realm?
options: human effort, spells, and supernatural power; the last two belong to the unconcentrated level, the desire realm
human effort, karmic action, and superior absorption; the first two belong to the unconcentrated level, the desire realm
karmic action, absorption, and seed; the first two belong to the concentrated level, the form realm
the elements' force, karma, and absorption, all of the formless realm
quiz.why: The treatise names human effort, karmic action, and superior absorption. Master Cháng Bǎi: the first two conditions belong to the unconcentrated level and refer to the desire realm; the third is the work of absorption. The five conditions listed next, for turning one result into another, are a separate list.

quiz.q: The English has "without a physical basis" for 若無所依. Is the added "physical" fitting? How does the treatise reject the three similes?
options: fitting: mind needs form to transfer to rebirth; an echo is illusory, a reflection's original has not ceased, and grasping an object involves no travel
unfitting: the support is the store-consciousness, not form; the three similes in fact hold, and "physical" should be deleted
unfitting: the support is one's parents; the treatise adopts the echo simile
fitting, but the treatise holds the intermediate state to be a shadow following the body
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: mind cannot transfer elsewhere to rebirth without the support of form; and if the original form has ceased, there is no image, so what shadow could move about? Thus "physical" is an addition that the lecture supports, and the English is better for it. Note its "since a reflection's original does not cease" is the reason a reflection is no model for one whose body has died.

quiz.q: When form arises, what takes hold of the location first?
options: derived matter takes it first, the elements then following, since derived matter is what the eye sees
particles take it first, and the elements then gather
consciousness takes it first, and form then arises from it
the elements take the location first, derived matter then occurring dependent on it
quiz.why: The treatise says the elements take hold of the location first, and other derived matter then occurs dependent on it; only the elements are present there as obstruction. Master Cháng Bǎi: the four elements first occupy an equal measure of the place where form is to arise. This supports the earlier point that derived matter shares one location with its elements.

quiz.q: "The earth-element and its result": how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 界 and 果?
options: 界 is the desire realm, 果 its ripened result; earth belongs only to that realm, the higher two having none
界 is seed, and 果 is the own-mark that makes up earth; earth is coarsest and wind subtlest
界 is a boundary and 果 is crops, which earth nourishes
界 is one of the eighteen elements and 果 is the body faculty
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: 界 is seed, and 果 is the own-mark that makes up the earth element; and the order of coarse to subtle is that earth is coarsest and wind subtlest. So the phrase pairs a cause and its manifest result. The English "earth-element and its result" keeps the words, but "element" hides the sense of seed.

quiz.q: When sound arises from its source, how does it fill the place where it is heard?
options: it arises there suddenly and completely, like a flame's brightness, not gradually spreading outward
like ripples it gradually spreads to the ear, slower with distance, and so is heard later far away
sound stays at its source, and the ear goes out to take it
sound continues constantly and is merely sometimes unheard
quiz.why: The treatise says sound arises wherever it is heard, suddenly and completely, like a flame's brightness, not arising gradually and spreading outward. Master Cháng Bǎi: light does not move gradually from its source to fill a room; it arises at once throughout. And sound does not persist continuously within a cluster of matter.

quiz.q: What is the space-element, and how, per Master Cháng Bǎi, do we know of it?
options: the same as unconditioned space, an unarising real entity existing apart from any form
derived matter under light and dark; through light and dark one knows of space, which also depends on clusters of matter
a fifth great element beyond the four, producing all form
a pure concept, unrelated to form
quiz.why: The treatise says derived matter under light and darkness is called the space-element, depending on a cluster of matter. Master Cháng Bǎi: the space-element too is form; we know of it through light and dark; such derived matter belongs to visible colour, with light and shadow. This differs from unconditioned space in the previous fascicle, which is the mere absence of form.

quiz.q: The English has "things like a chariot are felt to be destructible" for 彼覺可壞. What is destructible, and how is the English off?
options: what is destructible is the chariot's parts, for a broken part stops it, so the English is right and fits the argument about shape
what is destructible is the cognition of the chariot; once it is taken apart that cognition is gone, so it is provisional
what is destructible is the Dharma, the English omitting the subject
what is destructible is the driver, whom the English omits
quiz.why: The treatise gives this as a third reason that shape is provisional. Master Cháng Bǎi: then this cognition of the chariot no longer exists, and so such forms are provisional; no real mark of length can be found, nor any own-mark of the other shapes. It is the 覺, the cognition, that is destructible. "Felt to be destructible" makes the chariot the destructible thing.
